description: This line plot illustrates the relationship between sample token count and the number of shared experts for two samples across six different tasks. The x-axis, labeled “Sample Token Count,” is plotted on a logarithmic scale with tick marks at powers of two, ranging from 2^9 to 2^20. The y-axis, labeled “Shared Experts for Two Samples,” is linear and ranges from 2.0 to 6.0. Six distinct lines represent the different tasks: Intent (orange), Summary (blue), Law (yellow), Translation (purple), Code (gray), and Math (green). The Intent line starts at approximately 3.7 and rises to about 6.0. The Summary line begins at 2.0, rises sharply to a peak of about 4.5 at 2^12, then declines slightly before rising again to 6.0. The Law line starts at about 3.6, rises to a peak of approximately 5.7 at 2^13, then declines slightly before rising to 6.0. The Translation line begins at about 5.1, rises to a peak of approximately 5.7 at 2^13, then declines slightly before rising to 6.0. The Code line starts at 2.0, rises to a peak of about 3.7 at 2^13, then declines slightly before rising to 5.7. The Math line begins at about 3.7, rises to a peak of approximately 5.7 at 2^13, then declines slightly before rising to 6.0. All lines eventually converge near the top of the y-axis, around 6.0, for sample token counts greater than 2^17.
